text.tspan: A sealed piston-cylinder assembly with cross-sectional area
is filled with a mixture of combustible fuel droplets
and air. The piston has mass
and has nonnegligible friction with the cylinder. When ignited, the fuel explodes
into a gas with pressure
, pushing the piston upward. The forces acting on the piston are shown in the free-
body diagram. Which of the following is a correct mathematical expression for the acceleration of the piston as it
moves upward within the cylinder?
Answer A
Correct. By Newton’s second law, the acceleration of the piston can be found by dividing the net force
exerted on the piston by its mass. The net force exerted on the piston is found by summing the four
forces represented in the free-body diagram. The force exerted by a gas is calculated by multiplying the
pressure of the gas by the area of the piston. The force exerted by the gas in the cylinder is exerted in the
direction of the upward motion of the cylinder, so it is positive in the summation. The forces exerted by
friction, gravity, and the atmosphere are all directed opposite the motion of the piston, so they are
negative in the summation.
